doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Released in 1961, recording for Blue Note and failing health
summary: After jail, Ware cleans up during the drug panic, records for Blue Note with Grant Green and Hank Mobley, and his health fails.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When I come out, just before that, a great big snowstorm hit New York, and I'm out there in a summer suit; this was about in '61, and anyway, A Jones A was working over there at a hotel with somebody, and anyway, I come out and a friend of mine, Billy Howell, a trombone player, living on the upper West Side, he got me a room over there, and that's when they had what they call 'drug panic' -- couldn't find no drugs nowhere.

But that was good because I had a chance to clean up; my body got clean, and that's when I was doing a whole lot of recording for the Blue Note during that period, too. A I had done many things with Grant Greene, and I did some with Hank during that period, and I got myself together, and did I go out to Chicago again? This was about '61. In the summer, anyway, I did the thing with Clifford Jordan, started an album, and a few other things.
So I went on up there and my health started failing;
